text: Load-bearing walls transfer structural load from slab and beams down to the foundation and must not be removed without structural redesign.
Columns must be aligned vertically across all floors to ensure proper load transfer and structural stability.
Beam depth increases with span length to reduce deflection and improve structural strength.
RCC (Reinforced Cement Concrete) combines steel reinforcement with concrete to resist both compression and tension forces.
Slab thickness for residential buildings typically ranges from 100mm to 150mm depending on load and span.
Footings must be placed below the soil’s bearing capacity depth to prevent settlement and structural failure.
Earthquake-resistant buildings use shear walls, base isolation, and ductile reinforcement design to absorb seismic energy.
Shear walls are vertical structural elements that resist lateral forces caused by wind and earthquakes.
Plumbing systems should maintain proper slope in drainage pipes to ensure gravity-based flow without blockage.
HVAC systems require proper duct sizing and airflow balance to maintain indoor thermal comfort efficiently.
Electrical load distribution must be balanced across phases to avoid overheating and system failure.
Concrete curing must be maintained for at least 7 to 14 days to achieve optimal strength development.
Waterproofing is essential in bathrooms, terraces, and basements to prevent long-term structural damage.
Expansion joints are required in long concrete structures to handle thermal expansion and prevent cracking.
Soil testing is mandatory before foundation design to determine bearing capacity and soil type classification.
